hints.title: Lazy In-Order Obstacle
hints.text: Precomputing the entire in-order traversal into an array uses linear space upfront. How can pausing and resuming traversal on demand yield the smallest unvisited element while storing only height elements?

hints.title: Left Spine Stack Invariant
hints.text: An in-order traversal always visits the leftmost available node next. Storing the path of left children on an explicit list guarantees that the top element is always the next in-order value.

hints.title: Controlled Stack Traversal Procedure
hints.text: In the constructor, push all nodes along the left spine from root onto a list. For hasNext, return whether the list is non-empty. For next, pop the top node, push all left descendants of its right child onto the list, and return the popped node's value.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: tree height (log N balanced, N skewed)
N: number of nodes in tree (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Each node is pushed and popped exactly once across all next() calls, giving O(1) amortized time per call with O(H) auxiliary memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Flattening the entire tree to an array consumes O(N) memory upfront regardless of whether iterator is fully consumed.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(H) space versus O(N) space for full precomputation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Proving O(1) amortized complexity via aggregate analysis: 2N total stack operations over N elements.
